subject: Parity scoping: open models vs proprietary baseline — acceptance thresholds & test plan
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mercurypay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@mercurypay.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T17:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up from demo — parity scoping

Ben,

Great demo earlier — thanks to you and the team. Two quick asks as we scope an eval sprint:

1) we need a clear test plan and pass/fail criteria comparing our in-house baseline (finetuned proprietary) vs the open models you suggested. What metrics should we run?
2) rough timeline & who on your side runs the benchmarks; we have a small infra window next week for heavy runs.

Additional context: our baseline is tuned on internal transaction dialogues and has a behavioral QA pass rate of ~84% on our internal rubric. We want to know whether an open model + Redwood serving/quantization can approach parity within 5–7% of that metric across our test prompts.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of ML Engineering
MercuryPay
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mercurypay.com>
Cc: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@mercurypay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — parity scoping

Tom — really appreciate the clarity. High level response and attachments below.

Quick answers:
- Metrics: accuracy on labeled intents (micro-F1), helpfulness scoring on a 5-point rubric (human raters), factuality regression checks (precision@k for retrieval-augmented responses), latency at p90/p99 under your expected QPS. We'll provide a scoring spreadsheet.
- Candidate models to evaluate (open): Mistral-Instruct-34B, Llama2-Chat-70B (8-bit/quant), and a 13B distilled variant (for low-latency path).
- Our baseline comparison approach: run identical prompt bundles (you shared 300 prompts) through your proprietary model and each open candidate in Redwood's dedicated environment, capture output tokens, run automated metric scripts, then a 3-person blinded human review for borderline cases.
- Acceptance thresholds proposal (initial): within 5% absolute on micro-F1, average helpfulness delta <= 0.4 on the 5-point scale, and no more than 2 percentage points increase in hallucination rate. These are adjustable after the first 50 prompts.

I've attached a short parity playbook and a snapshot CSV with the first automated pass we ran on a seed of 50 prompts (see attachments). Links to the detailed plan and HubSpot deal are below.

Next steps (my suggested):
1) You confirm test cluster window (we can queue heavy runs Wed 7/21).
2) You share the full prompt bundle + any redlines for PII.
3) We run automated pass + human review; Redwood will own the run and produce a pass/fail matrix.

Attachments: [Attachment: parity_playbook.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)], [Attachment: benchmark_results_snapshot.csv (text/csv, 48KB)], [Attachment: prompt_set_v1.txt (text/plain, 22KB)]

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@mercurypay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mercurypay.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T01:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — parity scoping

Ben — thanks for the checklist. Couple of clarifications from product/security: 

- Can you confirm how Redwood will handle PII in the prompt bundle during the eval? We need either on-prem execution or redaction + synthetic substitution.
- For the human review: can we provide the raters or does Redwood provide blinded raters? We prefer a mixed panel with at least one internal SME for transaction semantics.

Also: are you able to run a controlled latency curve (vary QPS) so we know whether the 70B option meets our p99 SLA? If the 13B variant sacrifices <3% helpfulness but hits p99 goals, that might be an acceptable trade.

Appreciate it — I'll confirm infra window by EOD.

—Aisha
VP Product
MercuryPay

Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mercurypay.com>, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@mercurypay.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T21:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — parity scoping (run plan & thresholds)

Quick operational readout and attached mini-scripts.

What we'll run:
- Automated pass: 300 prompts (you provided) through: proprietary baseline (your env), Mistral-Instruct-34B, Llama2-Chat-70B quant, and Distil-13B. Each model at 3 temperature seeds.
- Metrics emitted: micro-F1 (intent labels), BLEU-like token overlap, helpfulness score proxy (automated heuristics) and hallucination flags (URL/KB mismatch).
- Latency sweep: QPS = {1, 5, 10, 25}; capture p50/p90/p99 and tail jitter.

Acceptance thresholds we propose (editable after 50 prompts):
- micro-F1: open candidate within 5 percentage points of baseline (your baseline = 84% → pass >=79%).
- Human helpfulness: mean delta <= 0.4 on 5-point scale (baseline mean 4.1 → pass >=3.7).
- Hallucination: no more than +2 percentage points higher than baseline.
- Latency: p99 under 350ms for the low-latency variant (Distil-13B path). If Llama2-70B exceeds p99 SLA, we'll test quantization and fallback routing for interactive queries.

Deliverables and timeline: automated CSV + perf graphs within 24 hours of run completion (target: 7/22 18:00 UTC). Blinded human review kickoff 7/23, final summary by 7/26.

Attachments referenced: [mini-benchmark-scripts.zip (text/zip, stub)]

Notes on PII: we'll accept redacted prompts (Mercury provides redacted + mapping file) or run within their VPC. If they prefer redaction, we'll run a substitution script to replace account identifiers with synthetic tokens prior to sending to shared infra.

I'll start the runs once Tom confirms the cluster window.

—Priyom
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
